comments.author: gravypod
comments.why: Demonstrates fake map listings used by locksmith scammers
comments.text: This video has a demo of what is happening: [VIDEO] Essentially if you make a bunch of fake listings all around the State you work in people who are desperate will search for "X near me" and if you have the most dots it will resolve to you. This means more panicked buyers which directly translates to way more money.

comments.author: richbell
comments.story: A man's pay-to-use toilet gag showed Google Maps can be used to track people
comments.why: Example of rampant fake local businesses
comments.text: It's rampant. Locksmiths, appliance repairs, flowers, you name it. Unfortunately, I have not had similar luck in reporting obviously fake businesses. [VIDEO]

comments.author: acatton
comments.story: “find a way to be a predatory squatter on a chokepoint” – Cory Doctorow
comments.why: CBC investigation of fake locksmith listings across Canada
comments.text: CBC's Marketplace did an investigation about this years ago. [VIDEO] TL;DW: this is widespread in most cities in Canada. Scammers just setup fake businesses on google to have your nearest locksmith be some generic chain. I would expect this to be the same for the US.
